findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Several pans on a shelf being stored as clean were observed soiled with remaining food debris and stickers. The PIC was shown and education conducted. They moved the items back to dish for re-cleaning. Reviewing of procedures and oversight of the dish cleaners is suggested to prevent future issues. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are completely cleaned prior to storage and re-use in the facility.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.citation_text:
4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. 

The cooler to the left of the fryers was observed holding TCS foods with internal temperatures of 48.5F. Due to the situation with the fryers and per the PIC this cooler is not likely to have been opened much since that situation kicked off two days ago. At this time the TCS foods are being discarded due to the situation taking place with the fryers. The cooler itself still needs to be functioning correctly and that is what this violation is for. A follow-up will be conducted in 10 days to ensure that the equipment has maintenance conducted and is functioning correctly.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114.

Multiple rags used for wiping counters were observed stored on the counters in the kitchen. The PIC was consulted and moved the rags back into the buckets of sanitizer to correct. Ensure that all wet rags are stored between uses in sanitizer of effective concentration to prevent the proliferation of biological pathogens.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

The “Imperial” hot box on the prep line was observed heavily soiled during this inspection. Per the PIC this item should be cleaned nightly by staff. This appeared to not be happening at the time of the inspection. The PIC was shown and instructed to maintain clean. The temperature inside of this was observed over 400F and biological contamination is not the concern. Pieces falling out of this equipment into the open sauces underneath was the concern and the impetus for maintaining this equipment clean at the time of the inspection. Ensure that all physical equipment is maintained clean at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.110 Using Dressing Rooms and Lockers. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions. 

1) An employee shirt was observed in a container of flatbreads on the prep line. 2) A purse was observed stored on a wire shelf over consumer foods. Both locations were shown to the PIC and the items moved to correct. The flatbreads were also discarded to allay the potential concerns related contamination concerns. Ensure that all employee personal items are stored so that contamination of consumer foods is mitigated.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD.

Multiple employees were observed to don gloves without hand washing. Education was conducted with the PIC and they were instructed to review when hand washing is required with their staff and conduct oversight as needed. Ensure that hand washing is conducted each time that it is required by the code.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

On arrival the hand sink across form the manager’s office was observed without soap. The PIC was shown and replaced the soap to correct the violation. Ensure that all hand sinks are properly supplied at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure.
findings.comment: Observed no hot water to be available upon arrival. Discussed with PIC, hot water was being serviced during inspection. Inspector will spot check facility within the following days to confirm hot water is available. Ensure facility has hot water available during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 5-103.11(B) Capacity. (B) Hot water generation and distribution systems shall be sufficient to meet the peak hot water demands throughout the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Observed bar hand sink to be holding multiple items. Discussed with PIC, items were removed from hand sink. Ensure hand sinks are solely being used for hand washing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed bar soda gun to be soiled with mold accumulation. Discussed with PIC, soda gun was cleaned and sanitized. Ensure equipment food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency that prevents accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Observed no sanitizer solution to be available at bar. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer solution was prepared and tested at 200 ppm Quat. Ensure a sanitizer solution is available at the bar during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Observed the following issues:
1)(Repeat) Freezer to the left of chicken breading station observed soiled with food debris. 
2) QB drawers observed soiled with food debris. 

Discussed with PIC, areas will be cleaned. Ensure staff is cleaning non food contact surfaces at a frequency that prevents food debris from accumulating.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed soup to be hot holding in a warmer at 120F. Discussed with PIC, warmer was filled with too many soup bags. 2 soup bags were removed and placed in walk in cooler, and the remaining bags were able to be fully submerged in warmer and ran a temperature of 145F. Ensure staff is aware of equipment limits, any TCS food being hot held must be at or above 135F.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed cold holding station holding sauces to be at 50F. Discussed with PIC, cooler was serviced during inspection. After technician serviced cooler, cooler ran a temperature of 40F. Ensure all TCS food being cold held are kept at or below 41F, and that all cooler equipment is working up to manufactures standards.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
findings.comment: Observed dish machine to not be draining into floor drain. Discussed with PIC, it appears a piece connecting drain to floor drain is missing. PIC will contact Ecolab regarding dish machine, ensure dish machine is properly draining into floor drain.
findings.citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed the ice bucket being used for bar drinks to not have a lid on it, and the soda gun hose was in direct contact with ice. Discussed with PIC, the correct lid of the ice was found and placed upon ice container. Ensure foods are protected to prevent any possible contamination. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the steak holding cooler and cake holding cooler to have an accumulation of food debris present. Discussed with PIC, ensure non food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency that prevents food accumulation. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
(REPEAT x2) Observed the dish machine area to be have an accumulation of mold present on the caulking. Discussed re-caulking with PIC. Much of the facility building issues from the last routine inspection were corrected. Ensure the above area is addressed. Correct by the next routine inspection. Repeat from the 3/11/24, 3/20/23, and 8/1/23 inspection. 

6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE.
